title: A Garden for the Oath
premise: Mirabel Vane, a scribe bound to the Thornfell temple by her family's debt, has spent years mapping smuggler roads in secret — until prayers to the old gods start being answered again, and the answers come through her. The god of oaths names her his herald and demands she free King Aldric, whose crown is a hollow vessel worn by a devouring spirit that has ruled through him for a decade. With the exiled oathbreaker Wren Calloway, Mirabel crosses the mountains gathering the three broken pieces of the king's original coronation vow. In the thirteenth moon's eclipse, Mirabel must choose: restore the true king at the cost of her own memories, or keep them and let the thing on the throne finish devouring him. She gives up her name instead — a third path the god never offered — unbinding both king and herself, though she ends the story remembering everything except who she loved first.
about_author: Paloma Eastwick is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing defunct religious orders before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted chapel in the northern hills, where she keeps bees and an unreasonable number of unfinished maps.

chapters.title: Ink Owed
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet her copying tithes in the Thornfell temple, chafing under her debt-bond, and secretly sketching smuggler routes in the margins of discarded pages. When a dying pilgrim's prayer to a forgotten god is answered — audibly — the temple elders panic. Emotional beat: restless longing cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: The God Who Answered
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The old god of oaths speaks through every written vow in the temple, and only Mirabel can read what he writes. He names her herald and shows her a vision: a king wearing a crown that eats. The temple abbot, terrified, tries to bind her silence. Beat: awe curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: An Oathbreaker's Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Calloway, exiled for breaking a knightly vow, runs contraband through the passes Mirabel has mapped. A temple bounty draws them together; Wren recognizes the vision as the truth of why they fled the capital. Beat: cynical self-protection meeting inconvenient hope.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The god explains the terms: the crown-spirit completes its devouring when the moon finishes its impossible thirteenth turn. Three fragments of King Aldric's original coronation vow, scattered across the mountains, are the only key. Wren agrees to guide her — for payment, they claim. Beat: dread with a deadline.

chapters.title: What the Debt-Bond Costs
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Breaking her bond means the debt falls to her younger sister, Sefa. Mirabel steals her own contract in a night raid on the scriptorium, burning it before witnesses. The abbot declares her apostate. Beat: grief disguised as resolve.

chapters.title: The First Fragment
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In a drowned shrine beneath a frozen lake, they retrieve the fragment of 'to protect.' The water shows each of them their worst memory; Wren sees the day they broke their vow, and Mirabel realizes Wren's exile was mercy, not cowardice. Beat: reluctant intimacy.

chapters.title: Prayers in the Passes
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Word spreads that the old gods answer again, and desperate pilgrims flood the smuggler roads seeking Mirabel as herald. She must ration miracles she doesn't fully control, and one answered prayer kills a man. Beat: the weight of being believed in.

chapters.title: The Crown's Hunters
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The crown-spirit sends Hollowed knights — people whose vows it has eaten — to retrieve the fragments. Among them is Wren's former sworn brother, still half-himself. They escape, but learn the spirit knows exactly where they're going. Beat: guilt sharpened into fear.

chapters.title: A Kingdom That Forgot Its King
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In a valley town, they find subjects who genuinely love their gentle, empty-eyed king and resent the 'heretics' who call him possessed. Mirabel watches Aldric from afar and glimpses the man flickering beneath. Beat: doubt about whether rescue is wanted.

chapters.title: The Second Fragment
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The fragment of 'to serve' lies in a war-crypt guarded by the ghosts of soldiers whose oaths the crown consumed. To pass, Wren must speak their broken vow aloud and mean the mending of it. Beat: an oathbreaker learning what oaths are for.

chapters.title: Sefa at the Border
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Her sister finds them, sent by the temple as bait — or spy. Sefa reveals the abbot plans to hand Mirabel to the Hollowed knights in exchange for the temple's protection. Beat: betrayal inside love.

chapters.title: Moonturn Vigil
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Trapped by weather, the group waits out a night when the thirteenth moon hangs visible at noon — the spirit's power peaking early. Mirabel dreams inside the god's memory and learns he once served a king too, and failed him. Beat: compassion for the divine.

chapters.title: The Abbot's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Hollowed knights arrive with the abbot. Sefa turns on the temple instead, buying Mirabel time with a forged writ. The abbot dies holding his own vow like a shield, and the god cannot save him. Beat: horror at what faith costs.

chapters.title: Roads Only She Knows
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Fleeing with knights behind them, Mirabel leads the group through unmapped smuggler cuts — her secret maps finally mattering. Wren admits they've known who she was since the lake shrine. Beat: trust earned in motion.

chapters.title: The Third Fragment
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The fragment of 'to love' rests in the ruined chapel where Aldric was first crowned. It cannot be taken — only given freely by someone who loves the king without having met him. Mirabel offers her dearest memory as payment. Beat: sacrifice foreshadowed.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The payment works strangely: Mirabel loses not a memory but her sense of which memories are hers. She wakes unsure whether her love for Wren is real or borrowed from the fragment. Beat: identity unraveling.

chapters.title: The Gates of Ashes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach the capital during the eclipse's approach. Wren uses their disgraced name to open a traitor's gate, walking back into the city that exiled them. Hollowed knights converge. Beat: homecoming as confrontation.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the throne room, the crown-spirit offers Mirabel everything — her debt erased, her sister safe, Wren pardoned — if she hands over the fragments. It shows her the truth: the god of oaths helped forge the crown long ago. Beat: the ground of belief giving way.

chapters.title: King Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Deep in the palace crypts they find Aldric's buried body-self, sustained by the last scrap of his own vow. He begs them not to save him if saving means the spirit escapes to another host. Beat: mercy versus duty made flesh.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Climax. Under the eclipsed moon, Mirabel speaks the reassembled vow — protect, serve, love — while Wren holds the Hollowed knights at the doors. The spirit offers its final bargain: her memories for the king's freedom. Beat: everything staked.

chapters.title: A Name Given Up
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Resolution begins. Mirabel refuses both offered choices and surrenders her name itself to the god, unbinding herself from every vow including her debt — a loophole no one foresaw. The crown crumbles; Aldric wakes, mortal and weeping. Beat: triumph laced with loss.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Oath
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, coda. Months later, a nameless woman tends a garden grown over the ruined throne room, planting it with the god's blessing. Wren visits daily, telling her their story so she can choose it again. On the last page, she plants something and says, 'I think I'd like to be called Mirabel.' Beat: love chosen, not remembered.
